text:
maria: heads up — saw a ~18% invoice delta for tenant batch processed at 10:00 UTC, looks correlated with the new priority-routing change that landed yesterday.
leo: ugh. do we have an example tenant id and event ids? can repro locally?
devon: sample tenant t-8472. ingest shows duplicate billing events where route.priority=high bypassed dedupe-window.
julie: confirm — our dedupe key right now is (client_request_id || fingerprint || event_id) but priority routing rewrites fingerprint to route_fingerprint which is not stable across proxies.
maria: exact. proxies A/B are normalizing route_fingerprint differently, so same logical request gets two different fingerprints and ends up billed twice.
infra-bot: deploy 2023-11-02T18:04 UTC applied: routing-priority-refactor v1.3. rollback candidate if needed.
leo: short-term mitigation: if route.priority changes, fallback to original fingerprint header if present. but that requires proxies to keep the old header. breaking change risk.
devon: alternative: change dedupe key to include stable attributes only: tenant_id + client_request_id + model_hash. Will catch most cases but fails when clients don't send client_request_id.
julie: we should avoid making client_request_id mandatory — SDKs in the wild won't be updated quickly. we need a compatibility plan.
maria: suggestion: add an optional billing_meta.event_guid that proxies can attach. processors treat it preferentially if present, otherwise keep existing fingerprint. that makes it non-breaking.
leo: how about timeline for that? proxies team needs 2 sprints to add header. processors change is trivial.
devon: big danger: backfills. If we change dedupe key semantics mid-stream, running a ledger reprocess/backfill may double-credit or drop events depending on which key was used during initial ingestion.
julie: to avoid that, we can introduce a dedupe_version in the event envelope. ledger only applies dedupe rules based on event.dedupe_version && stored dedupe_version. When we roll out, new events will set v2 and old events remain v1. Backfills must normalize to the original dedupe_version unless we run a migration plan.
leo: proposal: 4-step rollout:
1) emit billing_meta.event_guid from proxies (shadow header) for 1% tenants (canary)
2) processors run in "prefer_guid_shadow" mode: write metric but continue dedupe using legacy keys
3) after 1 week of stable metrics (dedupe_hit_rate, invoice_delta), switch processors to use event_guid for dedupe for those canary tenants
4) gradually ramp tenants and expose a console flag for "show staged invoice (uncommitted)" so support can see differences
maria: I like that. metrics to add: billing.ingest.dedupe_hit_rate, billing.ingest.event_guid_seen_pct, billing.invoice.delta_by_tenant_hour
sre-ops: add alert if dedupe_hit_rate drops >2% vs baseline for canary pool. also check for increase in late_retry counts since priority routing may reorder messages.
julie: console UX note: customers see "pending credits" vs "committed invoice" confusion. can we add a small badge "pending adjustments" and a hover explaining the canary/backfill effect? Product wants minimal noise.
leo: UI folks asked for a deterministic example to show in hover copy. Suggest: "Pending adjustments reflect events still in routing/aggregation windows; they may be reconciled in 1-24 hours." clear and non-technical.
devon: implementation detail: we need a temporary metric store to track shadow-guid to legacy dedupe correlations. simplest is a Redis bloom/hll per hour window, but we need it to be queryable for audits.
maria: for audits we want exact mappings for at least 72 hours. use a small write-to-s3 fallback: processors append correlation rows to s3/tenant=.../date=... as newline jsonl (only for canary tenants).
infra-bot: note: s3 write path requires new iam role for processors; infra ticket INF-4319 created.
leo: question on quotas: if dedupe changes, will quota counters double-decrement? We currently increment usage_bucket on ingest before dedupe. That's probably why some invoices already spiked.
julie: move quota decrement to "post-dedupe commit" path. But that changes critical path and could increase latency.
devon: alternative: keep current increment but make dedupe idempotent at ledger commit: on commit, if dedupe hit, emit a "usage_correction" negative event to reverse the increment. easier than pushing quotas post-dedupe.
maria: prefer usage_correction route — less risk to latency. we need to ensure correction events are visible in the console and in the per-route token breakdown to avoid confusing customers.
leo: action items:
- proxies: add billing_meta.event_guid header in shadow for canary tenants (INF-4320) — julie to coordinate
- processors: add prefer_guid_shadow flag and s3 correlation output for canary (PR draft by devon)
- ledger: support dedupe_version and enforce idempotency via correction events (leo)
- console: show "staged adjustments" view and add hover copy; add metric charts for dedupe_hit_rate (julie)
- infra: create IAM role and S3 lifecycle for correlation logs (sre-ops)
maria: timeline: aim for canary next Tuesday, ramp to 10% after 1 week if metrics stable. full rollout after 3 weeks and synthetic backfill testing.
julie: I'll draft the support playbook: how to explain pending vs committed lines to customers, how to look up correlation logs, and who to escalate to for invoice disputes.
devon: PR link coming: https://git.internal/redwood/ingest/+/b1234 — implements prefer_guid_shadow and s3 write. ping me for review.
leo: ok, going to add the dedupe_hit_rate grafana panel to the eng-platform dashboard and a pinned note for canary tenants.
maria: thanks all. keep thread updates small here so support can reference. :thumbsup:
infra-bot: ticket INF-4319 updated: role and s3 lifecycle rules added. assignee: @sre-ops.
